bullets.title: Semis/AI tape in freefall: six-session losing streak, 362 new 52-week lows, breadth worst of 2026
bullets.body: SPX fell another 2.02% Thursday (NDX -2.21%), its 6th consecutive down day since 1999, with only 38 S&P names green — worst breadth day of the year. 362 stocks hit 52-week lows Friday morning; NVDA -25.1% YTD, ORCL -52.6% YTD, IONQ -53.6% YTD. Pre-market futures recovered modestly (+0.88% S&P, +1.2% Nasdaq) but semis remain under heavy pressure with AMD -4.7%, DELL -4.5%, SNDK -8.2%, MRVL -5.8%.

bullets.title: New AI chip export controls hit Malaysia/Singapore/Indonesia/Brazil; UBS sees 1-2 GW demand stripped
bullets.body: Commerce Department IFR requires licenses for chip sales to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil — more restrictive than expected per Morgan Stanley. UBS estimates the new controls could strip 1-2 GW from current AI chip demand. Controls are widening beyond AI accelerators to consumer chips and foundry access for Chinese firms; TSMC and Samsung halted shipments of advanced chips (16nm and below) to Chinese customers pending compliance review.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness closes near-term risk-on; December 50bp hike probability rising, mirrors 2018 analog
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller suggested a 50bp December hike; Musalem and Jefferson also signaling hawkish stance. FOMC minutes showed almost all participants judging further hikes likely appropriate. 22V closed its short-VIX/long-risk trade citing aggressive Fed rhetoric shifting focus from growth to inflation; Morgan Stanley flags the 2018 analog risk of the Fed hiking into a growth slowdown, with P/E multiples higher now but expected growth of 16% vs 6% then.

bullets.title: AI capex ROI doubts and circular financing concerns are the core bear thesis, not fundamentals
bullets.body: Nvidia signaling pullback on 'bank of AI' role with neocloud commitments now tied to customer financing completion; zero capital deployed from the $500B Wall Street chip financing program. Market concerns center on durability of AI capex in 2027-2028, capital/regulatory constraints, and wealth-effect feedback loop. Hedge funds are in the 2nd percentile of net equity exposure on a 5-year lookback; six-week selling streak in semis is the longest on record.

bullets.title: Retail liquidating tech ETFs at record pace; SOXX hit -11.5z Thursday
bullets.body: Retail investors liquidated Tech ETFs at the largest-ever weekly rate (-2.0z); SOXX hit -11.5z on Thursday. Despite the selloff, NVDA dominated dip-buying with extraordinary early-day demand (+10z in first 30 minutes). JPM estimates VIX could decline ~20 points from Nov 20 through year-end based on 25-year seasonality, suggesting tactical bounce potential on OPEX (put-heavy ~$900B delta, 75% puts).

bullets.title: Bull case intact on fundamentals: NVDA raised FY28 guide to ~75% growth; semis trade at 11x 2028E
bullets.body: NVDA raised FY28 revenue growth guidance to ~75% from ~70% and Q3 beat with improved Q4 guidance; demand continues to exceed supply. Goldman Sachs AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings vs ~16x for the S&P 500, with consensus expecting 31% semis EPS growth in 2028. JPMorgan estimates the market is currently pricing negative semis EPS growth after 2027 — Deutsche Bank notes tech positioning consistent with negative EPS growth. S&P 500 price targets cluster around 8,700, implying 20%+ upside.

bullets.title: Texas data center permit moratorium and multi-state regulatory headwinds threaten 2028 capacity pipeline
bullets.body: Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa announced a data center permit freeze post-January 19; SemiAnalysis estimates this risks 30% of GW in 2028. Loudoun County approved a 12-month data center pause. Arizona AG requested a delay on a SpaceX $50B data center vote; North Carolina Governor calling to phase out public subsidies for data centers and AI companies. Senate passed energy permitting reform to accelerate projects, partially offsetting.

bullets.title: Nancy Lazar: AI cycle in mid-stage with peaking revenue growth, weakening FCF, and rising competition
bullets.body: PSC Macro's Nancy Lazar flags AI sector in mid-cycle with egregious inflation, rising costs, peaking revenue growth rates, weakening free cash flows, and emerging credit/excess capacity concerns. Korea semiconductor export business confidence is clearly declining. Taiwan semiconductor sales growth expected to slow from 108% y/y in 2026 to just 29% y/y in 2027; MSCI All World IT index growth decelerated from 69% y/y in June to 16% y/y currently.

bullets.title: AI user companies showing productivity gains and rising forward margin expectations vs. non-users
bullets.body: ~50% of S&P 1500 companies now use AI (up from 20% in 2024); AI users posted stronger YTD sales per employee growth than non-users. Forward net margin expectations for AI users continue to climb even as non-AI user expectations decline. Narrowly defined AI explains 22% of aggregate demand growth YTD; broadly defined AI explains 42%.

bullets.title: Google shifting ~1M TPU 8i units (20% of 2027 shipments) from Broadcom to MediaTek on power constraints
bullets.body: Ming-Chi Kuo reports Google is cutting 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series shipments by ~1M units (~20%), mostly the higher-priced 8i Max/Whalefish models, and increasing MediaTek-designed TPU 8t shipments. The shift is driven by frontier model development priority and tight data center power constraints — a negative read for AVGO's custom silicon revenue.

bullets.title: Hedge fund net exposure at multi-year lows; consensus 16% NTM EPS growth historically overstates when nets this low
bullets.body: US L/S hedge fund net exposure is at 41-42%, a 1-year low and in the 1st-8th percentile on a 5-year lookback. Historically, NTM S&P 500 EPS growth has been 5-10% when HF nets are at current levels, vs consensus expecting +16%. Stan Druckenmiller is short copper, noting extreme macro uncertainty. Citi equity trading (CETS) remains on the sidelines and is not dip-buying despite some valuation improvement (growth stock premium now 21% vs 77% in June).

bullets.title: Macro regime: 'Quad 4' — growth and inflation decelerating together; Fed hiking into slowdown raises policy error risk
bullets.body: OPCO flags a 'quad 4' macro regime with growth and inflation decelerating simultaneously; Fed appears to be hiking into a slowdown, raising policy error risk. 10-year yields fell double-digits this week while copper hit a 7-month low. Homebuilder sentiment is at the lowest in 14+ years; pending home sales at a 25-year low. Any relief rally from OPEX is expected to result in lower highs per OPCO.

bullets.title: Week-ahead macro: Core PCE Wednesday, PMI Monday, busy earnings (ADI, DELL, ADSK, WDAY) in truncated holiday week
bullets.body: Manufacturing and Services PMI data print Monday morning; core PCE for October prints Wednesday — the key inflation data point for the December Fed decision. Earnings include HPE/ZM Monday, ADI/BBY/DLTR Tuesday morning, ADSK/DELL/WDAY Tuesday post-close, and DE Wednesday. Markets close early Friday at 1pm ET for Thanksgiving.

bullets.title: Taiwan export orders at record but shipments peaking; double-ordering concerns mirror 1990s patterns
bullets.body: Taiwan October export orders rose +78.3% y/y to record highs, with US orders to Taiwan +96.3% y/y to $44.9B. However, actual shipment growth is peaking and orders may be inflated by double-ordering similar to 1990s patterns. World IT EPS momentum is expected through early 2027 but cooling thereafter.

bullets.title: Data center power/permitting emerges as the binding constraint on the AI buildout, not chip supply
bullets.body: Blackstone acquired a 75% stake in two AWS data center JVs for ~$5B at a 7% initial cap rate, signaling institutional capital chasing the space. AWS broke ground on a $7B Indiana campus. Arista announced new R4 platforms for distributed AI inferencing with up to 60% lower power consumption. The convergence of Texas permit freeze, Loudoun pause, and power grid constraints is making permitting — not silicon — the near-term bottleneck.

bullets.title: META's net GHG emissions surged 45%; re-evaluating 2030 net-zero target as AI buildout accelerates
bullets.body: META is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero target after net GHG emissions surged 45% last year due to rapid AI infrastructure buildout. Separately, META's halted Class-C share offering leaves a $60B+ hole in funding plans with trial potentially not starting until April.

bullets.title: Consumer holding up: October retail sales control group +0.6% m/m; BofA holiday spending off to strong start
bullets.body: Control group retail sales rose 0.6% m/m in October, better than expected, with August-September revised up 70bps. BofA data shows holiday spending off to a strong start with spending growth converging across income groups. WMT reported e-commerce +23% and marketplace GMV +50%, with November tracking 'really strong start' at ~+3%.

bullets.title: Mortgage market deteriorating: 30yr fixed at 7.28%, existing home sales -8.8% y/y, CMBS distress rising
bullets.body: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 7.28% (from 7.11% prior week); mortgage applications fell 2.3% w/w with refinance apps 54% lower y/y. Existing home sales fell 5.5% in October and 8.8% y/y. CMBS special servicing volume hit $69.53B (11.49% of outstanding loans); office delinquencies increased 17bps to 12.33% with 75% of maturing Class-A office CMBS loans requiring additional equity to refinance.

bullets.title: Euro-area consumer confidence ticked up to -16.9 in November; recovery thesis intact but fragile
bullets.body: Euro-area consumer confidence improved 1pt to -16.9 in November, matching JPM's forecast but still 1.5 standard deviations below long-term average. JPM expects consumption to expand at a weak but resilient 0.5% annualized pace this quarter, with recovery from Q1 2027 as the energy shock fades. Key downside risks remain persistent energy shock, labor market weakness, and re-tightening financial conditions.

bullets.title: Semis need 2028 estimate cuts to stabilize; buyside feedback sees uninvestible NVDA near-term on Jensen risk
bullets.body: Buyside feedback from Klein's dinner: AI/tech is in a self-reinforcing bear market unwind where every piece of news gets sold. 2028 semis estimates are viewed as too high and need cuts for a meaningful rally, though 1H27 cuts are unlikely given strong orders. NVDA described as 'uninvestible near-term' with major risk if Jensen departs; speculation he could join INTC. Capitulation rally possible on no news once sentiment reaches max negativity.
